answer: Under standard retail guidelines, you must submit a main reimbursement claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. However, under Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [5]. Note that archived 2024 guidelines listed a deadline of 15 days from the date of discharge [3].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on standard retail plans, unless explicitly waived in writing by Aurora [3][5]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][4][5].
As of 1 April 2026, there are 11,400 hospitals in the Aurora network across 780 towns [1].

On the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. If a claim is made, the bonus is not reduced and simply stops accumulating for that year only [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment because infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed under permanent exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Aurora Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the issue internally to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final internal response is unsatisfactory, or if they have not responded within 30 days of your original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

Across all plans, road ambulance is covered up to ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, under the Aurora Gold plan, air ambulance cover is available up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, with no separate waiting period required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policyholder can cancel their policy and return it for a refund [2][3]. It lasts 15 days from the receipt of the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. During this time, the policyholder receives a refund of the premium minus the proportionate risk premium for the coverage period, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation because of technological advance, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For an emergency admission under cashless processing, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, everything will not be paid [1][5]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured, or ₹10,000 per day [1][2]. Because a room tariff of ₹15,000 per day exceeds this limit, a proportionate deduction with an eligibility ratio of 0.667 applies, reducing the payable amount across eligible bill items [1][5].

Dependent parents can be added under the Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, but they are not permitted under the Bronze plan [1]. Adding your mother will affect the policy cost because the premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered, which often costs more than buying a separate individual policy for that parent [4].

Credit for the waiting periods you have already served will carry over, but only up to the sum insured (including accrued no-claim bonus) of your previous policy [1][2]. Any incremental increase in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on the excess amount [1][2].

A newborn is automatically covered from day one of birth within the maternity limit for the first 90 days [2]. To continue coverage beyond 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the newborn to the policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth [1]. Requesting this within the 90-day window provides guaranteed-issue coverage with no medical underwriting, whereas requesting it afterward results in the child being treated as a fresh applicant [1].

The out-patient benefit (OPD rider) is not available on the Bronze plan [1]. The provided sources do not contain specific information about physiotherapy sessions, so I don't have enough information in the provided sources to answer that.
On the Silver plan, a claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points, but does not reset it to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the coverage limit for a caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, you would have to pay ₹60,000 out of pocket [1].

No, knee joint replacement is not covered immediately unless it is required following an accident, which has no waiting period and is covered from day one [1][2][5]. For non-accidental cases, knee joint replacement is subject to a 24-month waiting period [1][5].

Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. However, the wellness discount (which provides up to 15% off at renewal) is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount permitted to exceed it [1][3][5].

Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider and will be denied [2][3]. Your only option is to file for reimbursement, which requires pre-approval and is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [1][3][5].

The timeline depends on the type of claim:

* For reimbursement claims under general claim timelines, you have **45 days** from the date of the query to respond, after which Aurora closes the claim [2][5].
* For motor insurance claims, the deadline to respond to an Aurora query is **30 days** from the date of the query [4].

According to current claim guidelines, a planned cashless admission must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2][3]. However, an archived timeline specifies a notification deadline of 48 hours before admission [1].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. If Aurora raises a query, the timeline clock restarts once the queried document is provided [1]. Under archived 2024 rules, this timeline was previously 30 days from the last document [3].
Aurora Gold has no co-payment (nil) at all ages [1]. Additionally, Aurora Silver has no co-payment for claims where the eldest insured member is below age 60 [2].

Across the four plans, pre-hospitalisation coverage is 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days, respectively [1]. Post-hospitalisation coverage across the four plans is 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days, respectively [1].

You should consider the **Gold** plan (or **Platinum** plan), as both cover dependent parents-in-law [1], and the Gold plan removes room-rent sub-limits [3]. Note that while Source [1] states that the Gold plan covers dependent parents-in-law, Source [4] specifies that the Gold family floater covers up to two dependent parents without explicitly mentioning parents-in-law [1][4]. Additionally, all Aurora Top-Up and Super Top-Up variants feature no room-rent sub-limits [2].

Dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded, unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3]. Additionally, out-patient dental work is not covered under any plan [1].

You lose your accumulated benefits—such as waiting periods restarting and accumulated no-claim bonuses being lost—if you do not renew before the grace period expires [2][3]. The grace period is 30 days from the renewal due date for annual policies and 15 days for policies paid in instalments [1][5]. Renewing within this grace period preserves your continuity unbroken [3].
No, denial of cashless access is not a rejection of your claim [1]. If cashless is denied, you can still submit a claim through the reimbursement route [3].

Completing the quit-tobacco programme earns 200 wellness points per year [2], which contribute toward a renewal-premium discount at a rate of 1,000 points = 5% (capped at 15%) [3].
